This indicates the mechanism (antigen directed cytotoxicity and checkpoint blockade) was at least partially engaged. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: Both arms failed to achieve meaningful clinical benefit. The monotherapy arm achieved only 7.7% ORR and 2.05 months PFS, while the combination arm showed similar results (7.7% ORR, 2.65 months PFS). These are poor outcomes for advanced melanoma, well below typical response thresholds. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: No subgroup analyses were reported, so we cannot assess differential responses within the population. 5. CONFOUNDERS: The trial was small (N=27) which may have limited power. The population was PD-1 refractory, representing a challenging treatment setting. High rates of serious adverse events (multiple SAEs >15% incidence) may have impacted treatment delivery, though no specific dose modifications were reported.
